name: The Lich's Spellbook
summary: On Brightwater Lake's island, a spellbook draws Bethor Iceshard's attention. He hopes its pages will reveal the lich's skill and who he was in life.

sections.title: A Reclusive Master's Tomes
sections.body: A free-willed lich guards an island in Brightwater Lake with skeletal minions. He distrusts the outside world and mistakes other undead for Scourge thralls, ordering his guardians to kill anyone who approaches. Bethor Iceshard seeks skilled necromancers for the Forsaken beneath Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. He sends an emissary into the island camp to take the lich's spellbook. Bethor hopes its pages will reveal the master's power and identity before death took Lordaeron.

sections.title: Unmasking Gunther Arcanus
sections.body: The recovered spellbook reveals that the reclusive lich is Gunther Arcanus, Bethor Iceshard's old friend and comrade-in-arms from before the Third War. Gunther was a necromantic prodigy in life, and his writings show that his power grew greater in undeath. Bethor knows Gunther could be a valued master of the dark arts for the Forsaken. Someone must first convince the suspicious lich that the Forsaken are free of the Lich King's grip.

faq.q: Where is the Lich's Spellbook found?
faq.answer: The spellbook lies in a container named Gunther's Books, in the encampment on Brightwater Lake's central island in northern Tirisfal Glades.
The book belongs to a free-willed, reclusive lich on Brightwater Lake's island. Bethor Iceshard hopes its pages will reveal the lich's identity and skill.

faq.q: Why does Bethor Iceshard want the book?
faq.answer: Bethor Iceshard wants to learn the lich's identity and measure his necromantic skill, hoping to recruit him for Lady Sylvanas and the Forsaken.

faq.q: Why does the lich attack visitors to his island?
faq.answer: The lich believes other undead nearby remain mind-controlled Scourge slaves. He orders his minions to attack anyone who approaches his island refuge.

faq.q: What does Bethor hope to learn about the author?
faq.answer: Bethor hopes to learn who the isolated lich was in life and whether his necromantic knowledge could aid the Forsaken.

angles.text: As an undead, you know that some who escaped the Lich King's control did not join the Forsaken at once. Rogue undead survivors across Tirisfal still distrust one another.
As a mage, you can see how the spellbook joins Dalaran wizardry with dark necromancy. Its author greatly expanded his craft after becoming undead.
